svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Location and Attachment of Rafters

g.text: Rafters directly opposite each other, tied
Opposite rafters tied at the peak
Rafters offset by their own thickness and
Offset rafters on a ridge board
Framing members are connected by gusset plates or nailing
at the peak in conformance with Table 9.23.3.4., except
Sentence (3) strips: not less than 200 mm by 75 mm by 0.41 mm
thick, spaced not more than 1.2 m apart, nailed at each end by

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Rafters are located directly opposite each
other and tied together at the peak, or may be
offset by their own thickness if nailed to a
ridge board not less than 17.5 mm thick.
Except as permitted in Sentence (3), framing
members are connected by gusset plates or
nailing at the peak in conformance with Table
Where the roof framing on opposite sides of
the peak is assembled separately, such as in
the case of factory-built houses, the roof
framing on opposite sides is permitted to be
fastened together with galvanized-steel strips
not less than 200 mm by 75 mm by 0.41 mm thick
spaced not more than 1.2 m apart and nailed at
each end to the framing by at least two 63 mm
nails.
Drawn: rafter pairs near the peak, gussets, ridge board and strips in yellow or grey. Strip position on the framing is illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.14.4. (page 9-219)
